Create Slope Index of Inequality (SII) for Deprivation Gap metric

derive_deprivation_gap.Rd

Create the deprivation gap, a percentage point difference in early diagnosis (ED) proportion, between the most and least deprived extremes. This can be applied across any number of other factors as specified with the by argument e.g., across ICBs and reporting period.

Usage

derive_deprivation_gap(ed_data, by, ed_prop_col, ed_denom_col, depr_col)

Arguments

ed_data

A data.frame with columns containing:

  • Numeric early diagnosis proportion.

  • Integer denominator of early diagnosis proportion, or number of staged cases.

  • String deprivation quintile.

  • Any other columns to group the data by.

by

A character vector naming columns in ed_data to group the data by, expected to be the reporting period and the geography.

ed_prop_col

String name of column in ed_data for the early diagnosis proportion.

ed_denom_col

String name of column in ed_data for the early diagnosis proportion denominator i.e., number of staged cases.

depr_col

String name of column in ed_data specifying deprivation quintiles across which to measure inequality.

Value

A data.frame with all columns specified in by, as well as values for the columns below for each of the groupings across by. This function use of nested data / list columns to keep the data and models grouped together. The main output is the sii column which contains the deprivation gap value.

data

List of data.frame: containing ED figures and anything else in input ed_data

sii_model

List of lm: The full models as fit on data.

sii_summary

List of summary.lm: summary() of models in sii_model

sii_coeffs

List of numeric matrix: coefficients() of the sii_model

sii_confint

List of numeric matrix: with 95% confidence intervals of coefficients of sii_model

sii

Numeric: SII value, taken as the gradient of the sii_model

sii_std_err

Numeric: Standard error of sii

sii_lci_95

Numeric: Lower 95% confidence interval for sii

sii_uci_95

Numeric: Upper 95% confidence interval for sii

Details

The calculations are done as follows:

  1. Scale deprivation quintile groups between 0 and 1. Each quintile is assigned to the midpoint of the proportion of the population it represents. For example, the first 20%, quintile 1, is placed at 0.1 (or 10%)

  2. Compute inverse variance of a binomial proportion to use as weighting for each subgroup. For deprivation quintile i, its weighting \(w_i\) is calculated from its early diagnosis proportion \(p_i\), and count of staged cases \(n_i\) as:

    $$w_i = \frac{n_i}{p_i(1 - p_i)}$$

  3. Build the weighted linear regression models for each group specified in by, through applying helper function fit_sii(). The linear model uses scaled deprivation quintile predicting early diagnosis proportion, weighted by the inverse variance.

  4. Take the SII as the coefficient of the scaled deprivation quintiles. That is, by scaling from 0 to 1, the gradient of the slope gives us the entire deprivation gap.

Examples

example_df <- data.frame(
  date = rep(as.Date("2026-02-01"), 5),
  icb_code = rep("ABC", 5),
  deprivation_quintile = c("1 - most deprived", "2", "3", "4", "5 - least deprived"),
  ed_prop = c(0.55, 0.58, 0.595, 0.606, 0.619),
  ed_denom = c(39546, 43663, 48796, 51117, 50739)
)

example_gaps <- derive_deprivation_gap(
  example_df,
  by = c("date", "icb_code"),
  ed_prop_col = "ed_prop",
  ed_denom_col = "ed_denom",
  depr_col = "deprivation_quintile"
)

example_gaps[1, "sii"]
#> # A tibble: 1 × 1
#>      sii
#>    <dbl>
#> 1 0.0804
